lesson.subject: science
lesson.title: Pushes, Pulls and Magnets
lesson.summary: Pushes and pulls are forces, and magnets pull on some metals.
learning_objectives: Say that pushes and pulls are forces
Test what a magnet picks up
Show that magnets attract and repel

standards.text: Compare how things move; notice that some forces need contact and magnetic forces act at a distance; observe how magnets attract or repel and attract some materials and not others

success_criteria: I can say if an action is a push or a pull
I can test what a magnet picks up
I can say when magnets attract and repel
lesson.real_life: Fridge magnets, a swing in the park, toy cars, and steel spoons and foil in the kitchen.

warm_up.prompt: You throw a ball. Is that a push or a pull?
A push or a pull is a force.
Which one sticks to a magnet?

blocks.markdown: Today's big question: what makes things move?
blocks.say: Today we find out what makes things move. What is a push, and what is a pull?

blocks.alt: An empty wooden swing with a pink seat hanging in a garden
blocks.caption: To start a swing you push it or pull it back. That is a force.
blocks.credit: Photo by Markus Spiske on Unsplash
blocks.say: This swing is waiting. What would you do to make it move?

blocks.markdown: A **push** moves things away. A **pull** brings things closer.
blocks.say: A push moves something away from you. A pull brings something towards you.

scenes.caption: A push.
scenes.say: You kick a football. Your foot pushes the ball away.

scenes.caption: A pull.
scenes.say: You open a drawer. You pull the handle towards you.

scenes.caption: A push.
scenes.say: You close a door. Your hand pushes it shut.

question.prompt: You kick a football. Is that a push or a pull?
question.hint: Which way does the ball go?
question.explanation: Your foot pushes the ball away from you.

blocks.markdown: A **force** is a push or a pull.
blocks.say: Pushes and pulls are both forces. A force can start, stop or change a movement.

scenes.caption: Push strength.
scenes.say: A big push sends a toy car far. A small push sends it a short way.

scenes.caption: A swing.
scenes.say: A swing needs a pull back and a push forward. Then it swings.

scenes.caption: Stopping.
scenes.say: A goalkeeper uses a force to stop the ball. Forces can stop things.

question.prompt: A bigger push sends a toy car farther.
question.hint: Think about pushing hard and gently.
question.explanation: The bigger the push, the farther the car goes.

blocks.title: Max the magnet robot
blocks.transcript: I am Max the robot. I love magnets and I love tests. I hold my magnet near a steel paperclip. Click! It sticks. An iron nail jumps to my magnet. Iron is magnetic. Foil is shiny, but nothing happens. It stays behind. My wooden pencil does not stick either. Wood is not magnetic. I hide the clip under paper. My magnet still pulls it. My two magnets push apart. Like poles repel each other. I sort my things. Magnetic ones go left. The rest stay right!
blocks.caption: A magnet-loving robot tests things in a toy room.

points: A bigger force can move things farther
blocks.say: Let us remember. Pushes and pulls are forces. They make things move, stop or change.

terms.meaning: A force that moves something away from you.
A force that brings something towards you.
A push or a pull.
A seat that moves backwards and forwards on ropes.
The player who stops the ball going into the goal.

blocks.markdown: A **magnet** pulls on some metals. Things it pulls are **magnetic**.
blocks.say: A magnet pulls on some things. We test things to find out which ones.

scenes.caption: Magnetic.
scenes.say: Hold the magnet near an iron nail. The nail jumps to the magnet.

scenes.caption: Not magnetic.
scenes.say: Try a wooden pencil. Nothing happens. Wood is not magnetic.

scenes.caption: Foil.
scenes.say: Try aluminium foil. It is a shiny metal, but it is not magnetic.

blocks.caption: Steel pins are made from iron, so a magnet pulls them. Test before you decide.

blocks.say: These steel safety pins are small. A magnet will pull on them.

blocks.markdown: A magnet works through thin paper.
blocks.say: A magnet can pull through thin paper. The force still reaches the metal.

blocks.title: Magnetic or not?

points: A magnet picks up iron and steel

blocks.say: Let us remember. Magnets pull on iron and steel. They do not pull on most other things.

terms.meaning: An object that pulls on some metals.

mini_quiz.explanation: We predict first, then test to check.

blocks.markdown: The ends of a magnet are called **poles**.
blocks.say: Every magnet has two ends. They are called poles. One is north and one is south.

scenes.caption: Attract.
scenes.say: A north pole and a south pole pull together. They attract.

scenes.caption: Repel.
scenes.say: Two north poles push apart. They repel each other.

scenes.caption: Like poles.
scenes.say: Two south poles also repel. Like poles push apart.

question.prompt: What happens when a north pole meets a south pole?
question.explanation: A north pole and a south pole attract.

blocks.markdown: Play the game, then answer a question.
blocks.say: Warm up your memory. Watch the magnets light up, then copy them.

blocks.goal: Watch the order, then copy it. It gets longer each time!
blocks.say: Watch the order closely. Then copy it.

question.prompt: Two north poles push each other away.
question.explanation: Like poles repel, so two norths push apart.

blocks.say: Let us remember. Magnets attract or repel. The force works without touching.

terms.meaning: One of the two ends of a magnet.
The two ends of a magnet, north and south.
To pull towards.
To push away.

blocks.say: Magnets do useful jobs every day. Many fridge doors close with a magnet inside.
Some toys use magnets to join together. Magnets hold train carriages in a line.

blocks.markdown: A big magnet lifts steel cans.
blocks.say: In Pakistan and the UK, recycling centres use big magnets too.
